verdict.rationale: Windmill's own docs list webhooks and HTTP routes as first-party triggers for scripts and flows. They also say flows expose webhook endpoints, including version-pinned ones, so external HTTP requests can start workflow runs. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of how the request payload maps to flow inputs, detail on custom URL paths for HTTP routes, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can expose a custom webhook URL that receives external HTTP requests and starts a workflow run with the payload

citations.quote: Use schedules, webhooks, emails, HTTP routes, websockets, Kafka, Postgres, NATS, SQS, MQTT, GCP, Azure Event Grid and more.
Flows additionally expose version-pinned webhook endpoints that target a specific flow version by its numeric version ID instead of the latest deployment.
